matches.title: Epigenetic landscape, key transcriptional regulators, and in vivo identification of human Tr1 cells [scMultiome]
matches.summary: Type 1 regulatory T (Tr1) cells are CD4+ T cells with immunoregulatory function, which are induced from mature peripheral CD4+ T cells in response to persistent extra-thymic antigens. The role of human Tr1 cells in disease is not completely understood, because transcription factors that regulate their antigen-driven differentiation are not known, and there is lack of consensus on how to best identify them in the tissue, where antigen interactions occur. Here, we leveraged comprehensive bulk and single-cell (sc) transcriptomic, epigenomic, and TCR repertoire profiling of human antigen-induced Tr1 cells, complemented with CRISPR-based functional genomics, to uncover the role of transcription factors IRF4, BATF and MAF in human Tr1 cell differentiation and function. In addition, we identify a Tr1 cell transcriptional signature that can reveal Tr1-like cells in sc-RNA-seq datasets of peripheral blood CD4+ T cells of patients treated with Tr1 therapy, and within tumor-resident CD4+ T cells in patients with clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, triple-negative breast cancer, and colorectal cancer. These data enable further development of Tr1 therapies and Tr1-targeting treatments, and provide new insights into human Tr1 cell biology.

matches.title: METIMMOX: Colorectal Cancer METastasis - Shaping Anti-tumor IMMunity by OXaliplatin
matches.summary: This study aims to determine the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of the sequential addition of immune-modulating therapy to standard-of-care therapy of microsatellite-stable (MSS)/mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Patients with MSS/pMMR-mCRC harbor tumor that can be transformed into an immunogenic disease by short-course oxaliplatin-based therapy, and may thereby benefit from the addition of immune-modulating therapy to improve outcome of the current oxaliplatin-based standard-of-care. Primary objective: To determine progression-free survival (PFS), in terms of failure of treatment strategy, of sequential treatment with the Nordic FLOX (5-Fluorouracil, oxaliplatin and leucovorin) regimen and nivolumab compared with the standard-of-care Nordic FLOX regimen in previously untreated MSS/pMMR-mCRC. Secondary objectives: To determine safety and tolerability of sequential treatment with the Nordic FLOX regimen and nivolumab compared with the standard-of-care Nordic FLOX regimen. To monitor and compare quality-of-life (QoL) alterations during therapy courses.

matches.title: Comprehensive Expression Profiles of mRNAs, LncRNAs, and CircRNAs in Colon Specimens of Patients with Slow Transit Constipation
matches.summary: Slow transit constipation (STC) is a complication of depression, which can be commonly seen, that can have a negative impact on STC patients’ prognosis and quality of life. Nonetheless, the pathogenesis of STC is principally uncertain. In this work, colon tissues from STC and non-STC patients were utilized to identify transcriptome expression patterns (mRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs) by high-throughput sequencing.

No cancer contrast is present, so it cannot serve as prior evidence for a tumor-vs-normal DE experiment.

matches.title: The high expression of siglec10 in tumor macrophages may promote the progression of colorectal cancer
matches.summary: SIGLEC10, also known as sialic-binding immunoglobulin-like lectin 10, is a member of the SIGLEC family. SIGLEC10 is expressed on the surface of immune cells and is involved in the regulation of immune responses by recognizing microorganisms or cells with specific sialic acids. Among other cancer types, SIGLEC10 has been identified as a novel tumor-associated macrophage-associated immune checkpoint. This study suggests that siglec10 is an independent prognostic factor in patients with CRC and may be a promising immunotherapeutic target for CRC in the future.

qc_pitfalls: Check for rRNA / globin carryover, especially in blood/plasma inputs.
Verify library size and 3' bias; low-input EV/exosome RNA often yields shallow, high-duplication libraries.
Normalization choice (median-of-ratios vs TMM vs CPM) changes DE calls — fix one and report it.
Batch/lane confounding with condition is the most common false-signal source; block or randomize.
Observed in GSE313035: low median library size (<1M counts) — typical of low-input / EV / exosome preps
projection.power_read: Planned N = 10 per group. Reasonable for moderate effects in bulk RNA-seq. Comparable prior studies used as few as 3 per group, so a detectable signal at N=10 is plausible if effect sizes match.

narrative: Public data does offer partial support for this plan: several human colorectal RNA-seq studies of tumor versus adjacent normal tissue already exist, the closest by match being GSE261033, GSE313035, GSE333496, and GSE245885, with GSE245885 sitting right at your intended ~10-per-group scale. However, the reanalyses came with important caveats. The datasets that were actually reprocessed (GSE313035 with 36 tumor vs 31 normal, and GSE285319 with 3 vs 3) provided only normalized expression tables rather than raw counts, so differential expression was estimated with a Welch t-test on log2 values instead of DESeq2, which weakens how directly those effect sizes translate to your design. QC also flagged a low median library size (under 1M counts) in GSE313035, consistent with a low-input/EV/exosome-style prep, and group assignments rested on file-arm labels rather than inspected clinical metadata. Notably, no genes came out as differentially expressed in two or more datasets under the concordance criteria, and the projection expects roughly zero significant genes at the stricter threshold. On the positive side, prior studies used as few as 3 per group, so N=10 is a reasonable size for moderate effects if your true effect sizes are comparable. Overall the feasibility read is cautionary rather than a clear green light: the biological question is well-precedented, but the available reanalyzed evidence is thin and method-limited, so I would confirm sample grouping and library quality before drawing strong conclusions.
